public_rationale: OpenAI introduced two successive models with higher token prices within six months. Those events support a broader reading that counts optional model upgrades. They do not establish two imposed increases for comparable existing service, which is the reading used here. Anthropic also held Sonnet pricing unchanged. Neither the contract record nor the wording is clear enough for a firm verdict.
limitations: The result depends on what counts as a price increase and how long the next few months lasts.
Unchanged public prices cannot exclude private contract changes.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI-native companies will see multiple price increases from model providers in the next few months.

statement.excerpt: Any product built on top of an AI model that shows any kind of success can be cloned immediately by OpenAI and Anthropic, and I believe that we’re going to see multiple price increases on AI-native companies in the next few months.
statement.document_title: This Is How Much Anthropic and Cursor Spend On Amazon Web Services

our_interpretation: The assessment addresses the normalized pricing forecast, not the separate assertion that successful products can be cloned immediately.
Multiple means at least two distinct pricing changes. One announcement affecting several customers counts once.
The surrounding discussion identifies OpenAI and Anthropic as the relevant model providers.

The ordinary reading is increased charges imposed on companies for comparable model access. Mandatory migrations and reductions in included access count; introducing an optional premium model does not automatically count.
I use six months after publication as a generous outer interpretation of the next few months, ending April 20, 2026. A three-month reading ends January 20, 2026.
criteria.support_condition: At least two distinct qualifying provider price increases affecting AI-native companies took effect within the interpreted horizon.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete pricing and customer-contract record shows fewer than two qualifying increases during that horizon.

evidence.excerpt: GPT‑5.2 is priced at $1.75/1M input tokens
evidence.explanation: The accompanying table lists GPT-5.1 at lower token prices, while the announcement says there are no current plans to deprecate it in the API. This establishes a more expensive successor option, not an imposed increase for existing access.

evidence.locator: Availability and pricing, opening paragraph and following price table
evidence.explanation: The price table lists GPT-5.4 at $2.50 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, above GPT-5.2. This supplies a second successor-model increase under a broader interpretation, but does not establish an imposed increase for comparable existing access.

evidence.locator: Introduction, paragraph describing availability and pricing
evidence.explanation: Anthropic kept this successor model's published token prices unchanged. That limits a general claim of rising prices but cannot disprove the existence of two increases elsewhere.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated contracts, invoices, or notices documenting at least two comparable-service increases during the horizon, or a sufficiently complete record showing fewer than two.
